title: 第92 章 半截好汉来自haimeine的打赏加更第 91章 集市判官来自koy11的打赏加更
slug: 杀妖涨修为道爷我成了
lines: “谢……谢大爷主持公道。”
大侠满意地点了点头，转过身去。
这时孙二娘正站在一旁，她方才付了钱，菜却没拿到手，心里很不痛快：
“大侠，您主持公道我无话可说。可您看，我的钱已经给了他们，菜却全被您的人拿走了。我包子铺明儿个还等着开张呢，您看这……”
大侠转过身，顺势伸手在她臀上摸了一把，嬉皮笑脸道：
“二娘莫急，这菜是百姓的，回头我让人给你送些到铺子里去。”
孙二娘在镇上是出了名的泼辣，当即把脸一沉，往后跳开一步，指着大侠的鼻子道：
“钱是我付的，你凭什么把菜拿走？你摸我一把也就算了，老娘不跟你计较，可那菜你得给我留下！”
大侠先是一愣，大约没想到有人敢当众顶撞他，当即咧嘴一笑。
“你付的钱？”
陈大侠盯着她看了两息，把脑袋凑到她跟前：
“真是你付的钱吗？”
孙二娘脸色变了。
她虽然泼辣，可到底只是个寻常妇人，对方是连县官都敢杀的煞星。
她攥紧了拳头，嘴唇哆嗦了半天，终于还是没忍住，颤声问了一句：
“你……你这和恶霸有什么区别？”
大侠闻言，仰头哈哈大笑。
笑完了，他环顾四周，目光扫过那些噤若寒蝉的百姓，朗声说道：
“当然有区别，区别就在于，洒家杀人，算是‘替天行道’。”
这话说得意气风发，理直气壮。
他说着环顾四周，目光从围观的人群脸上一一扫过。
被他看到的人，没有一个敢与他对视，纷纷低下头去，往后退，往两边散。
然后他猛地把脸一沉，忽然暴喝一声：
“看什么看？都给老子滚！”
集市上的人群霎时间作鸟兽散。
卖菜的扛起担子就跑，买菜的低着头疾走，连路边趴着的一条黄狗都夹着尾巴溜了。
方才还热热闹闹的早市，不过几息的工夫便散了个干净。
只余下两个人，还站在原地没有动弹。
陈大侠看见这个白发道士领着一个小丫头，直挺挺地杵在路当中，与四周仓皇散去的人群形成了鲜明对比。
四目相对。
陈大侠的眉头拧了起来。
这满街的人都散了，偏这一个不走，这就是不给面子。
他大步走上前来，身后几个随从也呼啦啦地跟了上来，一个个拿眼瞪着沈回。
有人把指关节掰得咔咔响，有人似笑非笑地打量着沈回身上那件衣裳，大约是在估摸这道士身上能刮出几两油水。
content_en:
"Thank you...thank you uncle for upholding justice."
The hero nodded with satisfaction and turned around.
At this time, Sun Erniang was standing aside. She had just paid, but she didn't get the food. She felt very unhappy:
"My hero, I have nothing to say for your justice. But you see, my money has been given to them, but all the food has been taken away by your people. My steamed stuffed bun shop is still waiting to open tomorrow. Look at this..."
The hero turned around, reached out and touched her buttocks, and said with a playful smile:
"Second mother, don't worry, this dish is for the common people. I'll have someone bring some to the shop for you later."
Sun Erniang was well-known as a shrewd woman in the town. She immediately lowered her face, jumped back, pointed at the hero's nose and said:
"I paid for it, why did you take the food away? Just touch me and forget it. I won't argue with you, but you have to keep the food for me!"
The hero was stunned for a moment. He probably didn't expect anyone to dare to contradict him in public, so he immediately grinned.
"What did you pay?"
Chen Daxia stared at her for a few breaths, then put his head in front of her:
"Is it really what you paid for?"
Sun Erniang's face changed.
Although she is fierce, she is just an ordinary woman, and the other party is a evil star that even the county magistrate dares to kill.
She clenched her fists and her lips trembled for a long time. Finally, she couldn't hold it back and asked in a trembling voice:
"You...what's the difference between you and a bully?"
Hearing this, the hero raised his head and laughed.
After finishing laughing, he looked around, glanced at the silent people, and said loudly:
"Of course there is a difference. The difference is that killing people in the Sa family is regarded as 'doing justice for heaven'."
This was said with high spirits and confidence.
As he spoke, he looked around, his eyes scanning the faces of the people watching.
No one he saw dared to look at him, they all lowered their heads, stepped back, and scattered to both sides.
Then he suddenly sank his face and suddenly shouted:
"What are you looking at? Get out of here!"
The crowd in the market suddenly dispersed.
The vegetable seller picked up his load and ran away. The vegetable buyer lowered his head and ran away. Even a yellow dog lying on the side of the road slipped away with its tail between its legs.
The morning market, which had been bustling just now, had dispersed in just a few breaths.
There were only two people left, still standing there without moving.
Daxia Chen saw this white-haired Taoist priest leading a little girl, standing upright in the middle of the road, in stark contrast to the crowds of people who were hurriedly dispersing around him.
Eyes facing each other.
Master Chen's brows wrinkled.
People all over the street have dispersed, but this one refuses to leave. This is a lack of face.
He strode forward, and several followers behind him followed suit, all of them glaring at Shen.
Some people cracked their knuckles, and some looked at Shen Hui's clothes with a half-smile, probably trying to estimate how many ounces of oil and water the Taoist priest could scrape off.
